presentingComplaint: Two to three weeks of worsening headache, low-grade evening fever and progressive drowsiness.
history: 34-year-old man, migrant construction worker from a high TB-burden region, with ~18 days of insidious frontal headache, evening-predominant fever, drenching night sweats and 4 kg weight loss. Over the last 4 days he has become increasingly drowsy and confused with two episodes of vomiting. Household contact treated for pulmonary TB last year. No prior antiretroviral therapy; HIV status unknown. No head injury, no recent travel outside India, unvaccinated status uncertain.
examination: Ill, thin, mildly drowsy (GCS 13, E3V4M6), oriented to person only. Neck stiffness with positive Kernig and Brudzinski signs. Right lateral rectus (CN VI) palsy causing horizontal diplopia. No papilloedema on this exam; no focal limb deficit. Chest clear. No skin rash. Pertinent negatives: no thunderclap onset, no petechial/purpuric rash, no lateralising motor deficit at presentation.

labs.CSF appearance: clear, forms fibrin web on standing

imaging: CT/MRI brain with contrast: basal meningeal enhancement, mild communicating hydrocephalus, no midline shift; chest X-ray shows an old right upper-lobe fibronodular scar suggesting prior/active pulmonary TB.
microbiology: CSF Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra positive, rifampicin resistance not detected; CSF AFB smear negative; CSF mycobacterial culture pending; bacterial Gram stain and culture negative; CSF HSV PCR negative.
citations: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on Tuberculosis: Treatment of Drug-Susceptible TB 2022
stewardship: Start standard 4-drug anti-tuberculous therapy: isoniazid + rifampicin + pyrazinamide + ethambutol (HRZE) with pyridoxine, plus adjunctive dexamethasone (tapered over ~6-8 weeks). Prolonged CNS regimen (2 months HRZE then 7-10 months HR). Empiric ceftriaxone may be co-administered initially until bacterial meningitis is excluded by culture.
contraindications: Isoniazid: give pyridoxine to prevent peripheral neuropathy; monitor for hepatotoxicity
Ethambutol: baseline visual acuity/colour vision, dose-adjust in renal impairment
Rifampicin: strong CYP450 inducer with major drug interactions; hepatotoxicity
Correct/monitor hyponatraemia (SIADH) with judicious fluid strategy
edgeCases: CSF Xpert Ultra can be negative in paucibacillary TBM — a negative test does not exclude it; treat empirically on clinical/CSF grounds
May present as tuberculoma with focal deficit/seizure rather than classic meningism
HIV co-infection can blunt CSF pleocytosis and worsen prognosis; always test HIV
expectedMaiK: Subacute lymphocytic meningitis with very high CSF protein, low CSF glucose, basal enhancement and hydrocephalus in a patient from a TB-endemic setting with a TB contact strongly indicates tuberculous meningitis; start HRZE plus adjunctive corticosteroids without waiting for culture, and confirm HIV status.
